office_does: The sheriff runs county law enforcement and the county jail for all of Ferry County.
race_blurb: Three-term Sheriff Ray Maycumber, a Ferry County peace officer for more than 25 years who is suing the State over its new sheriff-qualification law, faces former Ferry County deputy and 20-year Border Patrol agent Sam Olson of Curlew; both prefer the Republican Party. Olson led the August primary 1,281 to 995.

candidates.summary: Former Ferry County deputy and narcotics detective who spent 20 years with the U.S. Border Patrol, most of them in Curlew; first run for office.
highlights: Marine Corps 1993-1997; Ferry County deputy and task-force narcotics detective 1998-2005 [S1]
U.S. Border Patrol 2005-2025, a K9 handler in Yuma and Curlew [S1]
Promises 'an aggressive approach towards theft and drug abuse' [S1]

experience.basis: Has never held elected office and challenges a three-term sheriff, offering 'a fresh set of eyes', but brings 27 years in law enforcement, so the outsider case is partial.

safety.basis: His one stated operational priority is 'an aggressive approach towards theft and drug abuse' to protect homes and property; no treatment or diversion agenda.

candidates.summary: Ferry County Sheriff since January 2015 and a county peace officer for more than 25 years; a plaintiff in the sheriffs' lawsuit against the State's 2026 sheriff-qualification law.
highlights: Sheriff since 2015, after serving as Republic police officer, deputy and chief criminal deputy [S1]
Says the county cannot fund competitive hiring, hurting recruitment and retention [S1]
Respondent in the four sheriffs' suit against SSSB 5974; a court enjoined parts of the law [S1][S2]
Unopposed in 2022; trailed Olson in the August primary [S3][S4]

experience.basis: Three-term incumbent sheriff with more than 25 years as a Ferry County peace officer, running on that record.

safety.basis: Frames the office's needs as deputy hiring and retention and the funding to attract applicants; no prevention or diversion agenda, but no specific enforcement program either.
